thread:
maya: Heads-up: eval CI flagged a calibration shift on 'answer-agreement' after onboarding q4-llama-small. Can we triage?

eval-bot: Eval CI: metric 'answer-agreement' dropped 4.8% vs baseline on canary samples. Report: https://ci.internal/runs/12345

liam: Which change touched sampling or metric code in the last deploy?

sophia: I noticed a tiny change in the harness: PR abc123 toggled `--seed-mode=randomize` for the CI runner.

maya: Can someone run a deterministic sample with old harness vs new and diff the distributions?

rahul: Running quick local:
```
python tools/run_eval.py --model q4-llama-small --seed=42 --num=500
```

rahul: Results: old-harness (seed-mode=fixed) -> agreement 0.842; new-harness (randomize) -> agreement 0.801. Distribution histograms differ (more tail samples in new).

liam: OK, so it's sampling shift, not a quantization regression — that's a relief. Where did that seed-mode toggle land?

sophia: That change landed in eng-ml: PR 7820 (merged by me). The goal was to avoid stale deterministic caches in CI but I didn't anticipate metric sensitivity.

maya: @sophia please revert the sampling change in CI for now. Hold the q4-llama-small canary rollout until we confirm. :warning:

sophia: On it — reverting and re-running the canary. Revert command: `git revert abc123 --no-edit` then redeploy harness image.

eval-bot: Canary run finished: agreement delta now +0.1% vs baseline (within noise). Canary marked PASS.

maya: Thanks everyone. Action items: 1) keep determinist sampling in CI until we implement stratified/seeded sampling; 2) add a unit/regression test that fails on sampling-sensitive metric shifts; 3) follow-up PR to make sampling mode explicit per-eval job. I'll open the tickets.

liam: I can take the stratified-sampling task.

sophia: Sorry about the surprise — I'll add the regression test and docs for the PR.
